# Antenna grounding and SWR tuning basics

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Ground the antenna mount and connect the radio's red and black wires. [t2332]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Ground the antenna mount to a clean metal surface or run a separate ground wire.
2. Connect the radio's red wire to battery positive and black wire to the grounding source.

_Procedure reported by [t2332]._

## Tools

- [Partial] 12-gauge wire [t2332]

## Tips & gotchas

- Verify continuity from the mount directly back to the negative battery post. [t2332]
- Use a 47 SWR meter built into the radio for general readings, but expect it to be less sensitive than an external unit. [t2332]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Leaving a ground wire on when one was needed, or vice versa [t2332]
